blocks.text: How Enflite builds and changes its **SyteLine** forms: the project standards every change follows, and the platform behavior (personalization layers, **FormSync**) every developer should understand. The project SOP and shared step-by-step procedures live in [Enflite/Form-Project-Templates](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates). The [SyteLine Form AI Agent](/developers/form-ai-agent) turns the same SOP into an API: POST a form-customization request and the AI runs the template workflow for you.

topics.subtitle: How Enflite builds and changes SyteLine forms
topics.summary: Standards and platform notes for anyone changing Enflite's SyteLine forms.
topics.title: Developer

blocks.text: Every change to an Enflite **SyteLine** form follows these rules. They keep customizations upgrade-safe and reviewable. The full SOP lives in [Enflite/Form-Project-Templates](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates).

items: **TRN first, then production.** Everything is built and proven on **TRN**. Production repeats the same steps, in the same order, from the same files.
**Never change Infor-owned objects.** No edits to standard IDOs, tables, or Vendor forms. New fields go on user-extended tables (`Uf_ENF_*`); bigger features get a new table and a new IDO.
**Forms go in through FormSync at Site scope** — never over the Vendor definition, never by hand in Design Mode as the delivery method.
**Back up before every import.** Export the unchanged form from each environment into `original/` before the first import there.
**Never hand-edit a generated file.** Change the build script, re-run it, commit both.
**Preserve the file bytes.** Form XML stays UTF-8 with BOM and **CRLF** line endings, byte for byte.
**Mark what changed.** New and changed components are highlighted purple so testers can find them.
**Human review, always.** Form-project pull requests are never auto-merged.

blocks.text: What the repo is the source of truth for
The form repository (for example **Enflite/eCMRs**) says what is live. Keep this help in step with it: when a form changes, its help pages change in the same pass.

**FormSync** runs when **Infor** ships a new version of a form Enflite customized. It merges Enflite's **Site Default** changes with the new **Vendor** version instead of overwriting them.
Why it matters

items: Upgrades do not silently drop Enflite's form changes.

blocks.text: This is platform behavior, not something form users trigger. Developers planning a customization should expect a sync pass after each **Infor** upgrade and review any flagged conflicts before signing off.

topics.title: Project lifecycle
topics.summary: The seven phases every form project goes through, from scope to optimize.

blocks.text: Every form project follows the same seven phases. The runbook lives in the project's `docs/Implementation-Plan.md`; the shared step-by-step procedures live in [Enflite/Form-Project-Templates](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates) (`procedures/`).

head: Phase
What happens
rows: What changes, taken from the team's source: mockup, spreadsheet, or request.
UET types, fields, and classes, and how the form reaches each field.
On **TRN**: UET setup, Impact Schema, then the form through **FormSync**.
Confirm the fields are on the IDO before importing; then import and refresh.
Repeat the TRN steps in **production** in a scheduled window; smoke test.
Saves, reloads, new and existing records, grid columns, team sign-off.
Follow-up and bug fixes after two weeks live.

blocks.text: Gates that matter most

items: **Staging check:** confirm new fields are on the IDO (Design Mode property list, a throw-away Dataview) before the first form import.
**Launch:** use the **TRN** UET Excel exports as the checklist; end with a smoke test.
**Rollback:** re-import `original/<Form>.<env>.original.xml` through **FormSync**.

blocks.text: The detailed procedures — UET setup, FormSync backup and import, launch, rollback, new table + IDO — are in the [templates repo](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates/tree/main/procedures).

topics.title: New tables and IDOs
topics.summary: When UET does not fit: Enflite's pattern for a custom table and IDO, worked in eCMRs.

blocks.text: When a feature needs its own record and UET on an Infor table does not fit — Infor's key makes **New** impossible, or most fields would be read-only joins — build a custom table and IDO. The worked example is [Enflite/eCMRs](https://github.com/Enflite/eCMRs).
Two mechanisms, in order

items: **Table + IDO** first, built in **Application Studio** (project `ue_ENF`). **FormSync** cannot create these.
**Form** second, imported through **FormSync** once the IDO exists. It binds by the exact property names.

blocks.text: One master field list

Keep one field list in `scripts/` and generate everything from it: the table-columns CSV, the IDO-properties CSV, the form XML, and `docs/deploy-checklist.md`. Run the consistency check before every commit.
Build steps

items: Create the table and columns (**Application Studio** → **Tables**). The key column gets `AUTONUMBER(STEP(1))` so **New** works. `CreatedBy`, `CreateDate`, `UpdatedBy`, `RecordDate`, and `RowPointer` are generated automatically — do not add them.
Create the IDO on the table and add one property per column (or import the CSVs).
**Check In** the IDO (**IDOs** tab → the IDO → **Check In**). Property edits do not take effect until check-in.
Work through `docs/deploy-checklist.md` for the steps import cannot do.
Import the form through **FormSync**.

blocks.text: CSV rules

items: Match a fresh live export exactly: header names (including leading `*`), column count, and quoting. A mismatch fails silently.
SQL column **Data Type** must be a real type (`nvarchar`, `datetime`, `decimal`, `ItemType`) — never `String`.
Leave IDO **Property Class** and **Column Data Type** blank for custom properties.

blocks.text: Steps import never does

items: **Read Only**: re-import never changes an existing property's flag. Uncheck it in the IDO Properties grid, then **Check In**.
**Inline lists** (fixed drop-downs): set `ENTRIES(A,B,C)` on the property itself; leave **Property Class** blank.

blocks.text: Full procedure: [07-new-table-and-ido.md](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates/blob/main/procedures/07-new-table-and-ido.md).

topics.title: Adding IDM to a form
topics.summary: Connect a SyteLine form to Infor Document Management: the record's documents in the IDM Related Info panel.

blocks.text: When a SyteLine form is connected to Infor Document Management, the form's **IDM Related Info** side panel lists the documents that belong to the record you are on, and a file dropped into the panel is saved in IDM with the record's values on it. Worked example: [eCMRs](https://github.com/Enflite/IDM/blob/main/docs/ecmrs/Implementation-Plan.md), which looks up a CMR's documents by Item.
How the pieces fit

items: **Document type** (IDM): the kind of document and the attributes stored on each file. Enflite types are `ENF_<Area>Docs` with `AccountingEntity`, `EntityType`, `Description` plus the key attributes.
**Document type filter** (IDM): the `IDM-User` filter makes the type available. Users who cannot see the type will not see its files.
**Business Context Model** (IDM): links an *entity* name to the document type; its **XQuery** decides which files match the record.
**Form External Message Entities** (SyteLine): for one form, the entity it sends and which form property fills each attribute.
The form's **event handlers** (SyteLine): five handlers that send the record's values to the side panel each time a record is selected.

blocks.text: On every record, the form builds a JSON message from the entity row and posts it. IDM finds the Business Context Model for the message's entity, runs its XQuery with the message's values, and shows the matching files. Uploading a file does the reverse: the message's values become the file's attributes.
The steps

items: **Document type** (IDM): only if no existing type fits. Name `ENF_<Area>Docs`; add the key attributes (all `String`, single-value); add an ACL and **Set as Default ACL**.
**Document type filter**: add the type to the `IDM-User` filter.
**Business Context Model**: the entity name the form will send; the document type; the XQuery (file attributes start with `@`, form values go in `{}`); an auto **Description** for uploads.
**Form External Message Entities**: the form name, the entity, and one row per XQuery value — attribute names exactly as in the XQuery's `{}`, values `P(<form property>)`.

**Event handlers**: the five handlers go into the form XML through the project's build script, imported through **FormSync** at Site scope — never typed in Design Mode. Template: [templates/event-handlers.xml](https://github.com/Enflite/IDM/blob/main/templates/event-handlers.xml).
**Test on TRN**: open the form, check the message in **Context Viewer** → `InforBusinessContext` → JSON, upload a file, move records and confirm the panel follows.
**Production**: repeat steps 1-5 from the TRN setup, import the same form XML, smoke test, and record it in the project's README Release.

blocks.text: Gotchas

items: **Names are case sensitive everywhere** — attribute names in the document type, the XQuery's `{}`, and the entity row must match exactly.

Decide the **key** first: values unique to the record, or deliberately shared if documents should show on several records. A blank key value matches every file whose key is blank — make the key field required or add a second XQuery condition.

The fastest check for any "no files" problem is the browser's developer tools → **Network** → the panel's request to `idm.inforcloudsuite.com/ca/api/bc/search`: its body is the form's message, its response shows the exact **searchXQuery** IDM ran.

The Form Designer sometimes does not save a new event handler, and pasting a whole `SLFormExtMsgEntities...` response into a Method Call box fails — another reason handlers go in through the build script.

blocks.text: Full procedure: [how-to-add-idm-to-a-form.md](https://github.com/Enflite/IDM/blob/main/docs/how-to-add-idm-to-a-form.md). Troubleshooting: [troubleshooting.md](https://github.com/Enflite/IDM/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md). Every form connected to IDM: [forms.md](https://github.com/Enflite/IDM/blob/main/docs/forms.md).

topics.title: The SyteLine Form AI Agent
topics.summary: What the SyteLine Form AI Agent is, what it automates, and what it will never do.

blocks.text: Draft: the team has not confirmed this page yet.

The **SyteLine Form AI Agent** is how you ask the AI to customize a SyteLine form through an API instead of a chat session. You POST a form-customization request — the current form export, the IDO and SQL Table exports, and a list of instructions — and the backend AI runs the full [Form-Project-Templates](https://github.com/Enflite/Form-Project-Templates) workflow for you: backup first, TRN-first, UET-only field naming, byte-preserved form XML, and a review pull request at the end. The SOP knowledge lives in the agent; you never re-explain it.

Status (TBD): this API is documented from the accepted design (ADR-021 in the backend repo). The route implementation is still in flight — confirm the endpoints are live on your backend before building against them.
What it does

items: Scaffolds the form project repo from the template (`Enflite/<FormName>`).

Records the TRN and production **FormSync** exports in `original/` before anything is built — the rollback copies — and compares them byte for byte. If TRN and production have drifted, it stops and asks instead of guessing.

Builds `<Form>.xml` from the TRN original with the build script — never by hand — so every change stays traceable. New custom fields use UET-only `Uf_ENF_*` names, and every change is highlighted purple.
Writes the README, the implementation plan (with the UET design tables), the troubleshooting log, and the implementation-plan deck.
Opens a review pull request — then stops. `awaiting_review` is the agent's terminal state.

blocks.text: What it doesn't do

items: **Never merges a pull request.** Form-project pull requests are never auto-merged. A human reviews and merges; the merge is recorded under the human's name, and only then does the request become `completed`.
**Never touches SyteLine.** The TRN UET setup, staging checks, the FormSync import, TRN testing, the launch to production, and rollback stay numbered human steps in the generated implementation plan.

**Never starts without both rollback copies.** The TRN export comes with the request; the production export arrives as an attachment. If it is missing, the request waits as `blocked` — the agent never builds on a guess.
**Never invents requirements.** Vague instructions block with `invalid-requirements` instead of getting a creative interpretation.
**Never runs when the feature is off.** Both kill switches default off, so the whole family fails closed.

blocks.text: When to use it

Use it for changes that follow the standard form-project SOP — new fields, relabels, layout changes. The API drives the build; humans do the go-live. For anything outside the SOP, talk to the team first.

topics.title: Form AI Agent API reference
topics.summary: Endpoints, the five-input request contract, lifecycle, permissions, and the audit trail.

blocks.text: Draft: the team has not confirmed this page yet.

Versioned REST under `/api/v1/form-customizations`. Every endpoint requires authentication and the `syteline:forms` permission (Admin and AI Admin only — never the User role). Error shape everywhere: `{"error": {"code", "message", "requestId", "details?"}}`. The base host is TBD — the backend docs use a placeholder, so confirm the production API host before integrating.

Status (TBD): this API is documented from the accepted design (ADR-021 in the backend repo). The route implementation is still in flight — confirm the endpoints are live on your backend before building against them.
The five inputs
The requester supplies exactly these five inputs — nothing else. The SOP knowledge lives in the agent, not the request.

head: Input
Part name
Rules
rows: Exactly one (required); `.xml`; ≤ 10 MB; must parse as XML; the form name in the XML must match `formName`. This is the TRN export — the baseline the agent builds from.
Exactly one (required); `.csv`; ≤ 5 MB; UTF-8; header row with a property-name-like first column.
Exactly one (required); `.csv`; ≤ 5 MB; UTF-8; header row with a column-name-like first column.
Required; 1–100 items, each 1–500 chars. Be specific: field type, label, tab, position.
Optional; 0–20 files; ≤ 200 KB each (images, spreadsheets, PDFs, notes). A `*.production.original.xml` attachment is treated as the production FormSync original.

blocks.text: Submission shapes

items: **Multipart** (`multipart/form-data`) — preferred for large inputs. File parts (`formXml`, `idoPropertiesCsv`, `sqlColumnsCsv`, `attachments[]`) plus text fields: `formName`, `title`, `instructions` (a JSON array or newline-delimited text), optional `requestedBy`.

**JSON** (`application/json`) — the same contract inline: `formXml`, `idoPropertiesCsv`, `sqlColumnsCsv` as strings; `instructions` as a string array; `attachments` as `[{ filename, content }]` or `[{ filename, contentBase64 }]`; plus `formName`, `title`, optional `requestedBy`.

blocks.text: Endpoints

head: Method
Path
Does
Success
rows: Create a request from the five inputs
Full request record: status, step log, `resultSummary` or `blockedReason` + `blockedDetail`, and the `evidence` completion report on `awaiting_review`
List requests — `status` filter, `limit` (≤ 100, default 20), `cursor`. Admins see the tenant's requests; others see their own. This is the kanban-board query for form work.

head: Status
Meaning
rows: Work finished; review PR open. This is the agent's terminal state — the completion report and PR link live here
A human merged the review PR (never the agent)
Cancelled by the requester or an admin

blocks.text: Permissions and identity

items: `syteline:forms` — Admin and AI Admin only, never the User role. Requests are owned by the requester; identity comes from the auth context, never from request arguments.
Tenant-scoped: non-admins see only their own requests.
Privacy routing treats the family as `syteline.*`.

blocks.text: Audit trail

Every state change is audited — query with `GET /api/v1/audit?action=…` (needs `audit:read`): request created, runner started, each template step, blocked (with reason), awaiting review (repo + PR URLs), merged (human actor recorded), cancelled.

topics.title: Worked example: PO Detail Report Viewer
topics.summary: One full request: the PO Detail Report Viewer changes, what the agent does with them, and the completion report.

blocks.text: Draft: the team has not confirmed this page yet.

This page turns the recorded walkthrough of the **Purchase Order Detail Report Viewer** changes into one API request. The walkthrough's shape: back up first via FormSync, re-point the primary collection to the customized UE_FL-SL purchase order report collection with its custom load method, then add the Terms & Conditions group footer. The form name below is illustrative — use the exact name from your FormSync export.
The request

items: `formName` — the exact SyteLine form name from the FormSync export (letters, digits, underscores; must match the name inside the XML).
`title` — e.g. “PO Detail Report Viewer — collection re-point and Terms & Conditions footer”.
`formXml` — the TRN FormSync export: the baseline the agent builds from.
`idoPropertiesCsv` / `sqlColumnsCsv` — the IDO's properties and the backing SQL Table's columns.

`instructions` — (1) Change the primary collection to the customized collection from the simple report (UE_FL-SL purchase order report) and set the custom load method to match. (2) Add a Terms & Conditions group footer on the main flex layout: group property PO, page break before; region about 92 wide by 30 long; a nested flex layout with three proportional columns (1-3-1); a vertical flex with five static labels carrying the T&C captions; justification left; “no colon” on each static.
`attachments` — the production FormSync export (`*.production.original.xml`): the second rollback copy.

blocks.text: What the agent does

items: Backup first. Records both FormSync originals in `original/`, byte-preserved, and SHA-256 compares them. Identical → one `<Form>.xml` serves both environments; different → drift stops the build. The plan also records the walkthrough's scope decision: work in default scope directly, since the detail viewer is not in use yet — and marks changes to the live Purchase Order Report form as explicitly out of scope (those go live in a meeting, because they affect Purchasing immediately).
Re-points the primary collection to the customized UE_FL-SL purchase order report collection and sets the matching custom load method, then saves and regenerates — mirroring the walkthrough.

Adds the Terms & Conditions group footer: a new group-footer region on the main flex layout (group property PO, page break before), about 92 wide by 30 long; a nested flex layout with three proportional columns (1-3-1); a vertical flex with five static labels carrying the T&C captions, justification left, “no colon” on each. Every change is highlighted purple in the built `<Form>.xml`.

Writes the docs: README, implementation plan with the numbered human runbook steps, the troubleshooting log — including the walkthrough's gotcha (keep component names short; put long text only in the caption, or the save fails with a string-truncation error) — and builds the implementation-plan deck.
Opens the review pull request and stops. Status becomes `awaiting_review` — the completion report and PR link are attached.

blocks.text: The completion report

The `awaiting_review` record carries `resultSummary` (plain language: what was built), plus `evidence`: the form-project repo URL, the review PR URL, the `<Form>.xml` and deck artifacts, the recorded originals with their SHA-256 prefix, `openItems` (what the agent was unsure about — e.g. confirm the collection name against the simple report in the staging check), and `assumptions`.
What stays human

items: Import `<Form>.xml` into TRN through FormSync at Site scope, run the staging checks, test.
Merge the PR when it looks right — the request flips to `completed`.
Launch to production through the launch procedure; the recorded originals are the rollback path.

topics.title: Form AI Agent errors and blocks
topics.summary: Every error code and blocked reason, and the fix for each.

blocks.text: Draft: the team has not confirmed this page yet.
Two families: **HTTP errors** (the request was rejected — fix and resend) and **blocked reasons** (the request was accepted, but the agent needs a human — the record itself is the report).
HTTP errors

head: Code
Meaning
What to do
rows: Read `details` for the failing part and fix it.
Use the exact SyteLine form name: letters, digits, underscores.
Form customization is Admin/AI-Admin only — grant the role or have an admin submit.
Set it `true` and restart (see limits and flags).
A part exceeded its size limit
Read the completion report or blocked reason instead.

blocks.text: Blocked reasons
The record carries `blockedReason` plus human-readable `blockedDetail`. Nothing is half-built — the agent never imports anything anywhere.

head: Reason
What happened
What to do
rows: The current form `.xml` was not supplied or failed validation
Supply the TRN FormSync export as `formXml`.
No production FormSync export — the agent cannot complete the backup-first check
Export the same form from production FormSync and attach it (`*.production.original.xml`).
TRN and production originals differ — production has local changes
Decide which side is authoritative (template procedure 3), then create a follow-up request.
No GitHub token configured — the agent cannot create the repo or open the PR
Set `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the request can be retried.
The instructions could not be turned into a plan
Restate with field type, label, tab, position; verify `formName` against SyteLine.
An uploaded part tripped the malware boundary
Remove or replace the flagged attachment and create a new request.
Tooling issue, not a request issue — file it with the backend team, including the step log.

blocks.text: Reporting a problem
Include the request id and the relevant audit events. Never paste form XML containing customer data into a ticket.

topics.title: Form AI Agent limits and flags
topics.summary: Kill switches, rate and size limits, and the rules that never bend.

blocks.text: Draft: the team has not confirmed this page yet.
The Form AI Agent is fail-closed: everything that can turn it off defaults to off, and the rules below are enforced by the backend, not by convention.
Kill switches (both default off)

head: Variable
Default
Effect
rows: Master switch for the endpoints — off means every call fails fast with `403 FEATURE_DISABLED`.
Master switch for the agent runner — off means requests sit in `requested` and nothing runs.
Required to run: token with repo + PR access in the GitHub org. Missing → requests block with `missing-github-token`.
GitHub org for new form-project repos and PRs.
How often the runner picks up `requested` work.

blocks.text: Pull requests are never auto-merged
Hard rule, enforced by design: the agent has no merge capability. The review PR waits for a human; the merge carries a human's name, and only the human merge flips the request to `completed`.
Rate and size limits
Other guardrails

items: Permission-gated: `syteline:forms`, Admin/AI Admin only — never the User role. Tenant-scoped records.
Malware boundary: uploaded parts pass the same scanning as document uploads; a quarantine blocks the request (`attachment-quarantined`).
Backup-first is not optional: without both FormSync originals recorded, the agent does not build.
TRN/PRD drift stops the build — production's local changes are never silently overwritten.
Privacy routing treats the family as `syteline.*`.
